proposals.before: Na's great-grandson Ke Hui became Wei's western guardian general, colonel who pacified the Rong, and overseer of the western Qiang hosts.
proposals.after: Na's great-great-grandson Ke Hui became Wei's western guardian general, colonel who pacified the Rong, and overseer of the western Qiang hosts.
proposals.reason: 玄孫 means great-great-grandson (fourth generation), not great-grandson (曾孫).

proposals.before: Na's great-grandson Ke Hui served Wei as General Who Guards the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong, and Chief Commander of the Western Qiang.
proposals.after: Na's great-great-grandson Ke Hui served Wei as General Who Guards the West, Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong, and Chief Commander of the Western Qiang.
proposals.reason: 玄孫 means great-great-grandson (fourth generation), not great-grandson (曾孫).

proposals.before: Ma Heluo in Yizhong's ranks was a scholar; when Zhang Cao propped up Shi Shi he defected to become Cao's secretariat draftsman.
proposals.after: Ma Heluo in Yizhong's ranks was a scholar; when Zhang Chai propped up Shi Shi he defected to become Chai's secretariat draftsman.
proposals.reason: 豺 is read Chái; the name 張豺 is Zhang Chai, not Zhang Cao.

proposals.before: Among Yizhong's followers Ma Heluo was learned and literary; when Zhang Cao aided Shi Shi he abandoned Yizhong for Cao, who appointed him Gentleman of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Among Yizhong's followers Ma Heluo was learned and literary; when Zhang Chai aided Shi Shi he abandoned Yizhong for Chai, who appointed him Gentleman of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 豺 is read Chái; the name 張豺 is Zhang Chai, not Zhang Cao.

proposals.before: After Cao collapsed he crawled back, and voices clamored for his execution.
proposals.after: After Chai collapsed he crawled back, and voices clamored for his execution.
proposals.reason: 豺 refers to Zhang Chai (豺 read Chái), not 'Cao'.

proposals.before: When Cao fell he returned; all urged killing him.
proposals.after: When Chai fell he returned; all urged killing him.
proposals.reason: 豺 refers to Zhang Chai (豺 read Chái), not 'Cao'.

proposals.before: Shi Zhi's coup brought Xiang credentials as general who spreads might, Wuhuan colonel, Yuzhou inspector, and duke of Xinchang.
proposals.after: Shi Zhi's coup brought Xiang credentials as general of agile cavalry, Wuhuan colonel, Yuzhou inspector, and duke of Xinchang.
proposals.reason: 驃騎將軍 is the General of Agile (Swift) Cavalry; 'general who spreads might' mistranslates the office.

proposals.before: When Shi Zhi assumed title he appointed Xiang credential-bearing inspector, General Who Spreads Might, Colonel of the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.
proposals.after: When Shi Zhi assumed title he appointed Xiang credential-bearing inspector, General of Agile Cavalry, Colonel of the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.
proposals.reason: 驃騎將軍 is the General of Agile (Swift) Cavalry; 'General Who Spreads Might' mistranslates the office.

proposals.before: His staff took shape with Wang Liang of Taiyuan as chief clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui as marshal, Fu Zicheng and Heina of Lüeyang flanking the van and wings, Lian Qi of Nan'an on the right, Qiang Bai covering the rear, and Xue Zan with Quan Yi as advisers.
proposals.after: His staff took shape with Wang Liang of Taiyuan as chief clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui as marshal, Fu Zicheng of Lüeyang over the left division, Lian Qi of Nan'an over the right, Heina of Lüeyang in the van, Qiang Bai covering the rear, and Xue Zan of Taiyuan with Quan Yi of Lüeyang as advisers.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic text garbles the posts: 伏子成 commands the left division (左部帥) and 黑那 the front (前部帥); it also drops the origins of Xue Zan (太原) and Quan Yi (略陽).

proposals.before: When wanderers under Gu Yi seized Tangyi's interior minister Liu Shi and handed him to Xiang, the court reeled and named Zhou Min of the personnel ministry general of the central army to brace the Yangzi.
proposals.after: When wanderers under Guo Yi seized Tangyi's interior minister Liu Shi and handed him to Xiang, the court reeled and named Zhou Min of the personnel ministry general of the central army to brace the Yangzi.
proposals.reason: The surname 郭 is Guo, not Gu.

proposals.before: More than a thousand displaced persons led by Gu Yi seized Jin's interior administrator of Tangyi, Liu Shi, and surrendered him to Xiang; the court trembled greatly and appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min central army general to guard the river line.
proposals.after: More than a thousand displaced persons led by Guo Yi seized Jin's interior administrator of Tangyi, Liu Shi, and surrendered him to Xiang; the court trembled greatly and appointed Minister of Personnel Zhou Min central army general to guard the river line.
proposals.reason: The surname 郭 is Guo, not Gu.

proposals.before: Yao Chang, courtesy Maomao, ranked twenty-fourth among Yizhong's sons.
proposals.after: Yao Chang, courtesy Jingmao, ranked twenty-fourth among Yizhong's sons.
proposals.reason: The courtesy name 景茂 is Jingmao; 'Maomao' misreads 景.

proposals.before: Chang's courtesy name was Maomao; he was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
proposals.after: Chang's courtesy name was Jingmao; he was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
proposals.reason: The courtesy name 景茂 is Jingmao; 'Maomao' misreads 景.

proposals.before: He climbed through left guard general, a chain of western prefectures—Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Weiba, Brazil, Fufeng—three provincial inspectorships, a second tour as general who spreads might, colonel of foot, and the marquisate of Yidu.
proposals.after: He climbed through left guard general, a chain of prefectures—Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, Fufeng—three provincial inspectorships, a second tour as general who spreads might, colonel of foot, and the marquisate of Yidu.
proposals.reason: 武威 is Wuwei and 巴西 is Baxi commandery; 'Weiba' and 'Brazil' are corruptions, and the list is not all western.

proposals.before: He successively served as general of the Left Guard, prefect of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Weiba, Brazil, and Fufeng, inspector of Ning, You, and Yan, again General Who Spreads Might, colonel of infantry, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yidu.
proposals.after: He successively served as general of the Left Guard, prefect of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, and Fufeng, inspector of Ning, You, and Yan, again General Who Spreads Might, colonel of infantry, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yidu.
proposals.reason: 武威 is Wuwei and 巴西 is Baxi commandery; 'Weiba' and 'Brazil' are corruptions.

proposals.before: Xiang soon shifted to Beiqu to seize Guanzhong, camped at Xingcheng, sent his cousin Yao Lan, aide to the state, against Fucheng, and had his brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu rally Beidi tribes—more than fifty thousand households came over.
proposals.after: Xiang soon shifted to Beiqu to seize Guanzhong, camped at Xingcheng, sent his elder cousin Yao Lan, General Who Supports the State, against Fucheng, and had his elder brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu rally Beidi tribes—more than fifty thousand households came over.
proposals.reason: 輔國 abbreviates the title General Who Supports the State (輔國將軍), not 'aide to the state'; 從兄 is an elder paternal cousin and 兄 an elder brother.

proposals.before: Xiang soon moved to Beiqu, intending to take Guanzhong; he advanced and camped at Xingcheng, sent his cousin Yao Lan, aide to the state, to seize territory around Fucheng, and ordered his elder brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu to gather Rong and Xia of Beidi—more than fifty thousand households submitted.
proposals.after: Xiang soon moved to Beiqu, intending to take Guanzhong; he advanced and camped at Xingcheng, sent his elder paternal cousin, the General Who Supports the State Yao Lan, to seize territory around Fucheng, and ordered his elder brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu to gather Rong and Xia of Beidi—more than fifty thousand households submitted.
proposals.reason: 輔國 abbreviates the title General Who Supports the State (輔國將軍), not 'aide to the state'.

proposals.before: When the Qiang host closed in, Xiang flew into a rage, charged forward, and met them at Sanyuan.
proposals.after: When Deng Qiang's troops closed in, Xiang flew into a rage, charged forward, and met them at Sanyuan.
proposals.reason: 羌師 follows s0293, where Fu Sheng sent Fu Jian and Deng Qiang (鄧羌) to intercept Xiang; 羌 here most plausibly abbreviates Deng Qiang rather than naming the Qiang people, Xiang's own ethnicity.

proposals.before: When Chang usurped the title, he posthumously enfeoffed Xiang as Wei Wuwang and made Xiang's grandson Yanding Marquis of Dongcheng.
proposals.after: When Chang usurped the title, he posthumously named Xiang King Wu of Wei and made Xiang's grandson Yanding Marquis of Dongcheng.
proposals.reason: 追諡 confers a posthumous name, not an enfeoffment; 魏武王 is King Wu of Wei.

proposals.before: Staff filled out with Yin Xiang and Pang Yan as chief clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei as marshals, a corps of Tianshui aides—Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, Ren Qian—scribes Jiang Xun and Yan Zun, advisers Wang Ju through Zhang Qian, and column leaders from Wang Qinlu to Dang Shan.
proposals.after: Staff filled out with Yin Xiang and Pang Yan as chief clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei as marshals, a corps of Tianshui aides—Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, Ren Qian—scribes Jiang Xun and Yan Zun, advisers Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian, and column leaders Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, and Dang Shan.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic text collapses the adviser and commander lists into 'Wang Ju through Zhang Qian' and 'Wang Qinlu to Dang Shan', omitting eleven named appointees present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Chong's general Gao Gai marched fifty thousand south of Xinping and collapsed; Gai brought thousands over and won a supernumerary attendant's tile.
proposals.after: Chong's general Gao Gai marched fifty thousand south of Xinping and collapsed; Gai brought thousands over and won a supernumerary attendant's title.
proposals.reason: 'tile' is a typo for 'title' (拜散騎常侍, appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary).

proposals.before: In Taiyuan eleventh year Chang took the throne at Chang'an, declared amnesty, adopted era Jianchu and dynastic title Great Qin, and rechristened the metropolis with a court spelling that punned on Chang'an while invoking lasting peace.
proposals.after: In Taiyuan eleventh year Chang took the throne at Chang'an, declared amnesty, adopted era Jianchu and dynastic title Great Qin, and renamed Chang'an (長安) as Chang'an (常安, 'Enduring Peace').
proposals.reason: 改長安曰常安 renames the capital from 長安 to the homophone 常安; the idiomatic paraphrase obscures the actual new name.

proposals.before: At the Shanggui feast Gu Chengshan of Nan'an urged, "Our land is rich, rugged, and crowded with talent—made for war.
proposals.after: At the Shanggui feast Gucheng Shen of Nan'an urged, "Our land is rich, rugged, and crowded with talent—made for war.
proposals.reason: 古成詵: the surname is the compound 古成 (Gucheng) and the given name 詵 (Shen, as the text itself renders it in s0163/s0207); 'Gu Chengshan' misdivides and misreads the name.

proposals.before: Thereupon he feasted officers at Shanggui; Gu Chengshan of Nan'an advanced and said: "My province's people are prosperous and the terrain perilous; heroes stand thick as a forest—it is a land suited to arms.
proposals.after: Thereupon he feasted officers at Shanggui; Gucheng Shen of Nan'an advanced and said: "My province's people are prosperous and the terrain perilous; heroes stand thick as a forest—it is a land suited to arms.
proposals.reason: 古成詵: the surname is the compound 古成 (Gucheng) and the given name 詵 (Shen, as the text itself renders it in s0163/s0207); 'Gu Chengshan' misdivides and misreads the name.

proposals.before: Yin Wei and Yao Huang pressed Gu Chengshan: "Years later Deng still breathes; predators flock on every side; Chinese and tribesmen hedge—what next?"
proposals.after: Yin Wei and Yao Huang pressed Gucheng Shen: "Years later Deng still breathes; predators flock on every side; Chinese and tribesmen hedge—what next?"
proposals.reason: 古成詵: the surname is the compound 古成 (Gucheng) and the given name 詵 (Shen, as the text itself renders it in s0163/s0207); 'Gu Chengshan' misdivides and misreads the name.

proposals.before: Yin Wei and Yao Huang spoke to Gu Chengshan: "Fu Deng is a cornered foe yet years have not destroyed him; villains perch like owls everywhere rallying; Yi and Xia alike waver—what is to be done?"
proposals.after: Yin Wei and Yao Huang spoke to Gucheng Shen: "Fu Deng is a cornered foe yet years have not destroyed him; villains perch like owls everywhere rallying; Yi and Xia alike waver—what is to be done?"
proposals.reason: 古成詵: the surname is the compound 古成 (Gucheng) and the given name 詵 (Shen, as the text itself renders it in s0163/s0207); 'Gu Chengshan' misdivides and misreads the name.

proposals.before: Chengshan retorted, "Clear rewards and sure punishments win every able man—why fear the Di outlaw!"
proposals.after: Shen retorted, "Clear rewards and sure punishments win every able man—why fear the Di outlaw!"
proposals.reason: 詵 is the given name Shen (as rendered in s0163/s0207); 'Chengshan' misreads the compound surname 古成 plus 詵.

proposals.before: Chengshan said: "Our lord's stratagem knows no bound; trust rewards and certain punishments move all worthy men to joyful allegiance—why worry the great enterprise will not succeed or the Di bandit will not perish!"
proposals.after: Shen said: "Our lord's stratagem knows no bound; trust rewards and certain punishments move all worthy men to joyful allegiance—why worry the great enterprise will not succeed or the Di bandit will not perish!"
proposals.reason: 詵 is the given name Shen (as rendered in s0163/s0207); 'Chengshan' misreads the compound surname 古成 plus 詵.

proposals.before: Chengshan answered, "The triple Qin heartland is heaven's granary—our lord holds eight shares in ten.
proposals.after: Shen answered, "The triple Qin heartland is heaven's granary—our lord holds eight shares in ten.
proposals.reason: 詵 is the given name Shen (as rendered in s0163/s0207); 'Chengshan' misreads the compound surname 古成 plus 詵.

proposals.before: Chengshan said: "The three Qins are Heaven's storehouse; our lord already holds eight tenths.
proposals.after: Shen said: "The three Qins are Heaven's storehouse; our lord already holds eight tenths.
proposals.reason: 詵 is the given name Shen (as rendered in s0163/s0207); 'Chengshan' misreads the compound surname 古成 plus 詵.

proposals.before: Lan Niu of Fengyi broke with Fu Shinu under Murong Yong's hammer and cried for aid.
proposals.after: Lan Du of Fengyi broke with Fu Shinu under Murong Yong's hammer and cried for aid.
proposals.reason: 犢 is read dú; the name 蘭犢 is Lan Du, not Lan Niu.

proposals.before: Deng's prefect of Fengyi Lan Niu split from Fu Shinu; Murong Yong attacked him; Niu sent envoys begging rescue.
proposals.after: Deng's prefect of Fengyi Lan Du split from Fu Shinu; Murong Yong attacked him; Du sent envoys begging rescue.
proposals.reason: 犢 is read dú; the name 蘭犢 is Lan Du, not Lan Niu.

proposals.before: Lan Niu fell too, men and mounts included.
proposals.after: Lan Du fell too, men and mounts included.
proposals.reason: 犢 is read dú; 蘭犢 is Lan Du.

proposals.before: He also seized Lan Niu and gathered his soldiers and horses.
proposals.after: He also seized Lan Du and gathered his soldiers and horses.
proposals.reason: 犢 is read dú; 蘭犢 is Lan Du.

proposals.before: Years of stalemate and Deng's victories sapped loyalty—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mizijie Poluo, Zhao Edi, Liang Guoer and a handful kept the pledge, sons guarding baggage trains while fathers rode with Chang.
proposals.after: Years of stalemate and Deng's victories sapped loyalty—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mizijie Pochu, Zhao Edi, Liang Guoer and a handful kept the pledge, sons guarding baggage trains while fathers rode with Chang.
proposals.reason: 觸 is read chù; 彌姐婆觸 is Mizijie Pochu, not Poluo.

proposals.before: After Chang locked horns with Fu Deng year on year and repeatedly suffered Deng's defeats, near and far alike harbored plans to leave or join; only General Who Conquers Captives Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Assistant to the State Liu Guodan, Champion Might Mizijie Poluo, Dragon-General Zhao Edi, General Who Guards the North Liang Guoer and others kept faith undivided, all leaving sons to guard camps, supplying successive army grain, themselves leading picked troops to follow Chang on campaign.
proposals.after: After Chang locked horns with Fu Deng year on year and repeatedly suffered Deng's defeats, near and far alike harbored plans to leave or join; only General Who Conquers Captives Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Assistant to the State Liu Guodan, Champion Might Mizijie Pochu, Dragon-General Zhao Edi, General Who Guards the North Liang Guoer and others kept faith undivided, all leaving sons to guard camps, supplying successive army grain, themselves leading picked troops to follow Chang on campaign.
proposals.reason: 觸 is read chù; 彌姐婆觸 is Mizijie Pochu, not Poluo.

proposals.before: Chang was about to march to save them; Minister over the Masses Yao Min, left servant Yin Wei and others said to Chang: "Fu Deng is near Watting; Your Majesty ought not lightly move."
proposals.after: Chang was about to march to save them; Director of the Secretariat Yao Min, Left Supervisor of the Secretariat Yin Wei and others said to Chang: "Fu Deng is near Watting; Your Majesty ought not lightly move."
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Secretariat and 左僕射 Left Supervisor of the Secretariat; 'Minister over the Masses' (司徒) and 'left servant' mistranslate the offices.

proposals.before: Thereupon he left Minister over the Masses Yao Min holding Anding and night-raided Deng's baggage at Dajie, taking it.
proposals.after: Thereupon he left Director of the Secretariat Yao Min holding Anding and night-raided Deng's baggage at Dajie, taking it.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Secretariat, not 'Minister over the Masses' (司徒).

proposals.before: He then went to Qinzhou and locked horns with Wang Tong, Jian's inspector of Qinzhou; two-plus ten thousand households of Tujue Luochuan in Tianshui and Qiang Hu of Lüeyang answered Chang; Tong feared and surrendered.
proposals.after: He then went to Qinzhou and locked horns with Wang Tong, Jian's inspector of Qinzhou; more than twenty thousand households of the Tuge of Tianshui and Qiang Hu of Lüeyang answered Chang; Tong feared and surrendered.
proposals.reason: 二萬餘戶 is 'more than twenty thousand households', and 屠各 is the Tuge (Xiongnu) people, not 'Tujue Luochuan'.

proposals.before: At Qinzhou he faced Wang Tong until droves—Tujue herders in Tianshui, Qiang and Hu in Lüeyang—swelled his rolls; Tong yielded.
proposals.after: At Qinzhou he faced Wang Tong until droves—Tuge tribesmen in Tianshui, Qiang and Hu in Lüeyang—swelled his rolls; Tong yielded.
proposals.reason: 屠各 is the Tuge (a Xiongnu group), not the Tujue (Türks), who postdate this period.

proposals.before: Dou Yuan of the southern Qiang brought five thousand households and won western pacifier general.
proposals.after: Dou Yang of the southern Qiang brought five thousand households and won western pacifier general.
proposals.reason: 鴦 is read yāng; 竇鴦 is Dou Yang, not Dou Yuan.

proposals.before: Southern Qiang Dou Yuan led five thousand households to surrender and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
proposals.after: Southern Qiang Dou Yang led five thousand households to surrender and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
proposals.reason: 鴦 is read yāng; 竇鴦 is Dou Yang, not Dou Yuan.

proposals.before: Eastern guardian Gou Yao gripped Rebel-Wan keeps and connived with Fu Deng.
proposals.after: Eastern guardian Gou Yao gripped Niwan Fort and connived with Fu Deng.
proposals.reason: 逆萬堡 is a proper place name (Niwan Fort); 'Rebel-Wan keeps' translates the name element 逆 as a word.

proposals.before: General Who Guards the East Gou Yao held Rebel-Wan fort and secretly drew Fu Deng.
proposals.after: General Who Guards the East Gou Yao held Niwan Fort and secretly drew Fu Deng.
proposals.reason: 逆萬堡 is a proper place name (Niwan Fort).

proposals.before: After crushing Deng east of Anding he hosted a triumph; generals muttered, "Had General Wei Wuwang—your brother Yao Xiang—still commanded, Deng would be ash; you shut yourself in too tight."
proposals.after: After crushing Deng east of Anding he hosted a triumph; generals muttered, "Had King Wu of Wei—your late brother Yao Xiang—still commanded, Deng would be ash; you shut yourself in too tight."
proposals.reason: 魏武王 is Yao Xiang's posthumous royal title 'King Wu of Wei', not a general's title.

proposals.before: Fu Deng's General Who Spreads Might Moyifu led six thousand households to surrender and was appointed credential-bearing inspector, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Duke of Gaoping.
proposals.after: Fu Deng's General of Agile Cavalry Moyifu led six thousand households to surrender and was appointed Commissioned with Credentials, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Duke of Gaoping.
proposals.reason: 驃騎將軍 is General of Agile Cavalry, not 'General Who Spreads Might'; 使持節 is a commission with credentials, not an inspector post.

proposals.before: When Xing neared Kongkong Fort, Dou Chong's ring broke without a blow.
proposals.after: When Xing neared Hukong Fort, Dou Chong's ring broke without a blow.
proposals.reason: 胡空堡 is Hukong Fort; 'Kongkong' drops 胡.

proposals.before: By the time he reached Kongkong Fort of the Hu, Chong's siege dissolved of itself.
proposals.after: By the time he reached Hukong Fort, Chong's siege dissolved of itself.
proposals.reason: 胡空堡 is the place name Hukong Fort, not 'Kongkong Fort of the Hu'.

proposals.before: Deng heard Xing was bound for Kongkong Fort and withdrew; Xing thereupon raided Pingliang, took great booty, and returned—all as Chang had planned.
proposals.after: Deng heard Xing was bound for Hukong Fort and withdrew; Xing thereupon raided Pingliang, took great booty, and returned—all as Chang had planned.
proposals.reason: 胡空堡 is Hukong Fort.

proposals.before: Yang Fosong of Jin brought Di and Shu settlers to Chang; Yang Quanqi and Zhao Mu gave chase.
proposals.after: Yang Fosong of Jin brought more than three thousand Hu and Shu households to Chang; Yang Quanqi and Zhao Mu gave chase.
proposals.reason: The source says 胡蜀三千餘戶 (over 3,000 Hu and Shu households); 'Di' confuses the households with his title 護氐校尉.

proposals.before: Reaching Chang'an he summoned Grand Commandant Yao Min, Left Minister Yin Wei, Right Minister Yao Huang, Minister Di Bozhi and others to enter and receive testamentary charge to assist government.
proposals.after: Reaching Chang'an he summoned Grand Commandant Yao Min, Left Supervisor of the Secretariat Yin Wei, Right Supervisor Yao Huang, Minister Di Bozhi and others to enter and receive testamentary charge to assist government.
proposals.reason: 尚書左僕射/右僕射 are the Left/Right Supervisors of the Secretariat.

decisions.reason: 那玄孫柯回 uses 玄孫, the fourth-generation descendant (great-great-grandson), not 曾孫 (great-grandson). The proposed kinship term is accurate.
The literal field repeats the same kinship error: 玄孫 is great-great-grandson. The replacement matches the Chinese.
The person is 張豺; 豺 is Chái, not Cáo. Replacing Cao/Chai in this sentence restores the name without changing the rest of the rendering.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 張豺之輔石世也，背弋仲歸豺

decisions.reason: Literal 張豺 / 歸豺 likewise requires Zhang Chai and Chai, not Zhang Cao and Cao.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 張豺之輔石世也，背弋仲歸豺，豺以為尚書郎

decisions.reason: 豺敗 names Zhang Chai’s fall. 'Cao' is a wrong reading of 豺; 'Chai' is the correct short form.
The literal 'When Cao fell' mistranslates 豺敗; Chai is the right name.
石祗 appointed Xiang 驃騎將軍, General of Agile Cavalry, not a 'general who spreads might' (that would be 揚武). The office name is the real error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以襄為使持節、驃騎將軍

decisions.after: When Shi Zhi assumed title he appointed Xiang Commissioner Bearing Credentials, General of Agile Cavalry, Colonel of the Wuhuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, and Duke of Xinchang.
decisions.reason: 驃騎將軍 is General of Agile Cavalry, so the proposed cavalry title is right, but 使持節 is a credential, not an inspectorate; 豫州刺史 is the inspector post. The after still called 使持節 a 'credential-bearing inspector'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以襄為使持節、驃騎將軍、護烏丸校尉、豫州刺史、新昌公

decisions.reason: The Chinese assigns 伏子成左部帥, 斂岐右部帥, 黑那前部帥, 強白後部帥, and gives 太原薛贊 and 略陽權翼 as 參軍. The original garbles those posts and drops the two origins; the replacement restores them.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 略陽伏子成為左部帥，南安斂岐為右部帥，略陽黑那為前部帥，強白為後部帥，太原薛贊、略陽王權翼為參軍

decisions.reason: 流人郭斁: the surname 郭 is Guo, not Gu.
The same 郭斁 requires Guo Yi in the literal field.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 流人郭斁等千餘人執晉堂邑內史劉仕降於襄

decisions.reason: 萇字景茂: 景 is Jing, so the courtesy name is Jingmao, not Maomao.
The literal courtesy name must likewise be Jingmao for 景茂.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 萇字景茂，弋仲第二十四子也

decisions.reason: The prefecture list is 隴東、汲郡、河東、武都、武威、巴西、扶風. 武威 is Wuwei and 巴西 is Baxi; 'Weiba' and 'Brazil' are corrupt, and the commanderies are not all western.

decisions.reason: Literal Weiba/Brazil are the same corruptions of 武威 and 巴西; Wuwei and Baxi are the correct names.

decisions.after: Xiang soon shifted to Beiqu to seize Guanzhong, camped at Xingcheng, sent his elder paternal cousin Yao Lan, General Who Supports the State, against Fucheng, and had his elder brother Yi and General Wang Qinlu rally the Rong and Chinese of Beidi—more than fifty thousand households came over.
decisions.reason: 輔國 is the abbreviated generalship, 從兄 an elder paternal cousin, and 兄 an elder brother, so those proposed fixes are real. The after still renders 北地戎夏 as 'Beidi tribes', dropping 夏.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣其從兄輔國姚蘭略地鄜城，使其兄益及將軍王欽盧招集北地戎夏

decisions.reason: The literal replacement correctly expands 輔國 to General Who Supports the State and 從兄 to elder paternal cousin, while already keeping 戎夏 as Rong and Xia.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣其從兄輔國姚蘭略地鄜城

decisions.reason: After 苻堅、鄧羌等要之, 會羌師來逼 uses 羌 for Deng Qiang’s force, not the Qiang people (Xiang’s own ethnicity). Reading 羌師 as Deng Qiang’s troops is the sense the sequence requires.
追諡魏武王 confers a posthumous title, King Wu of Wei, not an enfeoffment (封 is used only for 延定).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 萇僭號，追諡魏武王，封襄孫延定為東城侯

decisions.reason: The Chinese names six 參軍 (王據 through 張乾) and nine 帥 (王欽盧 through 黨刪). Collapsing them to 'through/to' omits those appointees; restoring the names is required.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王據、焦世、蔣秀、尹延年、牛雙、張乾為參軍，王欽盧、姚方成、王破虜、楊難、尹嵩、裴騎、趙曜、狄廣、黨刪等為帥

decisions.reason: 拜散騎常侍 is an office title; 'tile' is a typo for 'title'.

decisions.after: In Taiyuan eleventh year Chang took the throne at Chang'an, declared amnesty, adopted era Jianchu and dynastic title Great Qin, and renamed the capital Chang'an to Chang'an, 'Enduring Peace'.
decisions.reason: The source does rename the capital (改長安曰常安), so the original paraphrase is incomplete, but the proposed after cannot stand: it inserts Chinese graphs into the English field. The revised line states the new name in romanization with the meaning 'Enduring Peace'.
南安人古成詵: 古成 is the compound surname and 詵 the given name Shen. 'Gu Chengshan' misdivides the name.
The literal field has the same misdivision of 古成詵; Gucheng Shen is the correct English name.
尹緯、姚晃謂古成詵: the addressee is Gucheng Shen, not Gu Chengshan.
The literal vocative is likewise 古成詵 and must be Gucheng Shen.
詵曰 uses the given name Shen. 'Chengshan' is a leftover from the misread compound surname.
Literal 詵曰 should be 'Shen said', not 'Chengshan said'.
The next 詵曰 is the same speaker Shen.
Literal 詵曰 again names Shen, not Chengshan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 詵曰：「三秦天府之國，主上十分已有其八。

decisions.reason: 蘭犢: 犢 is dú. Lan Niu would be 牛; the name is Lan Du.

decisions.reason: 犢遣使請救 continues the same name 蘭犢 / Du, not Niu.
又擒蘭犢 is capture of Lan Du, not Lan Niu.

冠威彌姐婆觸: 觸 is chù, so Pochu, not Poluo.
